It’s probably understood or taken that the Cleveland Browns QB1 position could be filled either by Shedeur Sanders or Deshaun Watson Otherwise, why would analysts suggest trade options for Dillon Gabriel?The new Browns head coach, Todd Monken, is keeping it [who is QB1] under wraps.Yes, the examining time is at its peak now; it may be higher when the 2026 preseason and season commence.But till then, it’s taken as Sanders or Watson could be QB1, and whoever is not, could end up being the backup.Leaving ample space open for Dillon Gabriel to play and be productive elsewhere. Just speculation here.Bleacher Report’s Moe Moton suggests a trade that the Cleveland Browns could consider. The trade involves sending Dillon Gabriel for a 2027 late-round pick.An interesting idea for this trade suggestion could be sending Gabriel to the Atlanta Falcons. Why? Let’s chalk out.Dillon Gabriel knows the Atlanta Falcons head coach, Kevin Stefanski. Stefanski was the head coach at Cleveland in 2025.The Atlanta Falcons quarterback room is full of lefties – Tua Tagovailoa and Michael Penix Jr. Gabriel is left-handed, too.Also, if injury concerns pile up for Michael Penix Jr. , Dillon Gabriel could step up and hold the fort.As for Tua Tagovailoa, though, they say it is a battle between the two QBs for the QB1 role.Tua Tagovailoa may be favored for the starting job. Because the pressure will be high on him as he is on a one-year prove-it deal.According to 92.9 The Game’s Abe Gordon, the former Miami Dolphins quarterback could start in Week 1. Penix Jr. may not be ready for Week 1.“I think the quarterback competition begins Week 1 based on Tua’s in-game performance,” Abe Gordon said.“If he is good, the quarterback competition does not begin. If he is bad, that’s when it begins. Whenever Penix is a full go in season and Tua’s bad.”If Tagovailoa underperforms, the Falcons may look at Penix Jr. , who is a former first-round pick rehabbing a torn ACL.And if injuries pile up as they did in 2025, and Kirk Cousins had to step up, Dillon Gabriel could be that person. All speculation again!Gabriel threw for 937 yards, 7 touchdowns, and 2 interceptions with a 59.5 completion percentage.According to Bleacher Report’s Moe Moton, a team in need of a primary backup could be willing to take a chance on him.Bleacher Report’s Kristopher Knox gave Dillon Gabriel a projected trade value of a 2027 seventh-round pick and suggested the Atlanta Falcons as the best trade fit.Dillon Gabriel is a better fit for former head coach Kevin Stefanski than for the current offense at Cleveland.His athletic limitations were on display last season, but he earned an 80.8 passer rating in six starts.According to The Athletic’s Zac Jackson, the Cleveland Browns will only trade Dillon Gabriel if they feel they can get something of consequence in return.There’s a scenario in which the primary competitors for the starting job stay healthy [Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders] and 2026 sixth-round rookie Taylen Green makes a real push for a roster spot.This could force the Cleveland Browns to make a decision on Dillon Gabriel in late August. But keeping four quarterbacks on the 53-man roster is possible.And it’s too early to know how Taylen Green will perform. Or even how much opportunity he will get on the gridiron.Deshaun Watson will be on the active roster even if he doesn’t win the starting job because the Cleveland Browns can’t afford to cut him under the league’s salary cap rules.But the depth chart and the rest of the quarterback room’s makeup are unsettled.
Article Summary: Cleveland Browns could send quarterback Dillion Gabriel to Atlanta Falcons for 2027 late round pick. Atlanta Falcons quarterback room is full of lefties – Tua Tagovailoa and Michael Penix Jr. Gabriel threw for 937 yards, 7 touchdowns, and 2 interceptions last season.

Article Title: 5 richest former NFL cheerleaders of all time: How Teri Hatcher, Stacy Keibler and others built multi-million-dollar fortunes
Article Text:
5 richest former NFL cheerleaders of all time: How Teri Hatcher, Stacy Keibler and others built multi-million-dollar fortunes(Getty)

1. Teri Hatcher : The 49ers Cheerleader Who Became One of Hollywood's Biggest Stars



2. Stacy Keibler : From the Ravens Sidelines to Wrestling and Television Success



3. Lisa Guerrero: From NFL Cheerleader to Award-Winning Journalist

4. Charisma Carpenter: Chargers Cheerleader Turned Television Favorite





5. Brandi Redmond : Reality Television Helped Grow Her Fortune

What do these former NFL cheerleaders have in common?



Being an NFL cheerleader is a dream for many people. It offers the chance to perform in front of packed stadiums and represent some of the biggest teams in American football. But cheerleading alone rarely leads to great wealth. For a few women, however, it became the first step toward something much bigger.Some found success in Hollywood. Others built careers in professional wrestling, television, journalism, or business. Over the years, they turned the recognition they gained into long lasting careers worth millions. Here is a look at five of the richest former NFL cheerleaders of all time and how they built their fortunes.Teri Hatcher tops this list with an estimated net worth of around $50 million as per Celebrity Net Worth. Before becoming a familiar face on television and in movies, she was part of the San Francisco 49ers Gold Rush cheerleading squad during the 1980s.Cheerleading was only a small chapter in her career. Soon after, she began landing acting roles in shows such as The Love Boat and Star Trek: The Next Generation. Her breakthrough came in 1993 when she was cast as Lois Lane in Lois & Clark: The New Adventures of Superman. The role made her one of television's biggest stars.She continued that success with a role as Paris Carver in the James Bond film Tomorrow Never Dies. Years later, she reached another career high by playing Susan Mayer in Desperate Housewives. The hit ABC series ran for eight seasons and earned her a Golden Globe Award, Screen Actors Guild Awards, and an Emmy nomination. More than four decades after cheering on NFL sidelines, Hatcher remains one of the most successful former cheerleaders in league history.Per Celebrity Net Worth, Stacy Keibler has an estimated net worth of about $25 million after turning a short cheerleading career into a long run in entertainment.She joined the Baltimore Ravens cheerleading squad in 1997 when she was just 18 years old. Not long after, she entered the world of professional wrestling through WCW before becoming one of WWE's most recognizable female stars during the early 2000s. Keibler later expanded her career beyond wrestling. She appeared on “Dancing with the Stars”, made guest appearances in sitcoms including “How I Met Your Mother”, and worked as a television host and model.The popular cheerleader has also invested in business projects while continuing to appear in entertainment. Her career shows how quickly opportunities can grow after stepping away from professional cheerleadingLisa Guerrero took a very different path from most names on this list. Instead of focusing on acting or reality television, she built her reputation in sports broadcasting and investigative journalism.Guerrero began as a cheerleader for the LA Rams during the 1980s. After leaving the sidelines, she stayed connected to the NFL by serving as Director of Entertainment for both the Atlanta Falcons and the New England Patriots. She later moved into television, working as a sports reporter before becoming an investigative journalist. Guerrero became widely known through Inside Edition, where she reported on major stories across the United States.Alongside journalism she also appeared in several television shows and films during her career. Now, her estimated net worth stands at around $30 million as per Lifestyle Net Worth, making her one of the wealthiest former NFL cheerleaders ever.Before becoming a familiar face in popular television dramas, Charisma Carpenter spent time as a cheerleader for the San Diego Chargers. Her acting career took off after she landed the role of Cordelia Chase in Buffy the Vampire Slayer. The character quickly became a fan favorite and later continued in the spin-off series Angel, where Carpenter played a leading role for several seasons.She later appeared in many other television shows, including Charmed, Veronica Mars, and The Lying Game. Carpenter also featured in several movies, including The Expendables series. Her steady acting career over more than three decades has helped her build an estimated net worth of around $4 million as per Celebrity Net Worth. While smaller than some others on this list, it remains an impressive achievement after starting as an NFL cheerleader.Brandi Redmond first became known as a member of the famous Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders. After leaving the squad, she found a completely different audience through reality television.She rose to national attention after joining The Real Housewives of Dallas. The Bravo series introduced viewers to her personal life and helped make her one of the show's most recognizable personalities. Outside television, Redmond has also been involved in business ventures and charitable work. Together with her family, she has explored different business opportunities while maintaining a public profile through social media and television appearancesHer estimated net worth is around $4 million to $5 million as per Nicki Swift. Although her path was different from the actresses and journalists on this list, she successfully turned her early NFL experience into a career that extended far beyond football.Even though they followed very different careers, all five women share one thing. Cheerleading was only the beginning of their journey. Their wealth did not come from performing on NFL sidelines. Instead, each of them spent years building new careers, taking on bigger opportunities, and growing their public profile long after their cheerleading days had ended.Some became award-winning actresses. Others found success in wrestling, reporting, or reality television. Each used the opportunities that came after cheerleading to create a lasting career and grow their financial success.Their stories also show that becoming an NFL cheerleader can sometimes open unexpected doors. While only a small number reach this level of fame, Teri Hatcher, Stacy Keibler, Lisa Guerrero, Charisma Carpenter and Brandi Redmond prove that life after the NFL can be just as successful as life on the sidelines.
Article Summary: Teri Hatcher tops this list with an estimated net worth of around $50 million as per Celebrity Net Worth. Stacy Keibler turned a short cheerleading career into a long run in entertainment. Brandi Redmond rose to national attention after joining The Real Housewives of Dallas.

According to CBS Sports’ Bryan DeArdo, Jadeveon Clowney seems a good fit for the Green Bay Packers.Mainly because Micah Parsons’ Dec. 2025 knee injury will probably sideline him for the start of the season.While Clowney is not like Parsons, he has continued to produce even after turning 30.Last year, Clowney played for the Dallas Cowboys, where he recorded 41 total tackles [24 solo], 8.5 sacks, and 1 forced fumble in 13 games.The 33-year-old edge defender generated 40 total pressures as a pass rusher that included 9 sacks, 29 hurries, and 2 QB hits, according to PFF.He gained an impressive 80.6 PFF pass-rush grade, which ranked him 15th among 115 qualified edge defenders.If it’s not the Green Bay Packers, then maybe the New England Patriots or the Chicago Bears could consider him? Let’s find out how.According to Bleacher Report’s Kristopher Knox, Jadeveon Clowney is the best fit for the New England Patriots.He could never play up to draft-pick status [No. 1 overall in the 2014 NFL Draft].But he became a very disruptive run defender and a solid late-career pass-rusher-for-hire option.He played last season for the Dallas Cowboys, where he played just 13 games and recorded 12 tackles for loss and 22 quarterback pressures, according to Pro Football Reference.The veteran edge defender has never recorded double-digit sacks, but he has at least 5.5 sacks in the last three seasons.As for why he is ideal for the New England Patriots? The franchise added Dre’Mont Jones and drafted Illinois edge Gabe Jacas.But the Patriots recorded just 34 sacks as a team in 2025. The stats were before they parted ways with K’Lavon Chaisson in free agency.K’Lavon Chaisson is with the Washington Commanders now.According to Da Windy City’s Casey McAleer, Jadeveon Clowney could be an inexpensive option for the Chicago Bears.Clowney could make all the difference to Dennis Allen’s defense. He would not just bring bags of experience but also come at a discounted price.According to Spotrac’s calculated market value, the edge defender is projected to sign a one-year, $5.7 million contract.His last contract was for $3.4 million. His total career earnings are $100 million.He is still a free agent in July. He is looking for a new home. Could Chicago be that?Even USA TODAY’s Tyler Dragon picked the Bears as the perfect fit for Clowney.Dayo Odeyingbo had just one sack and 10 pressures in 2025. He is slated to start alongside Montez Sweat. The Bears need more pass rush juice on the outside.The 33-year-old pass rusher Jadeveon Clowney could be that solution for Chicago. He still has some pass-rush sizzle left in him.He produced an average of 7.8 sacks and 43 total tackles over the past three seasons playing for the Baltimore Ravens, Carolina Panthers, and Dallas Cowboys.Could it be the Packers, Patriots, or the Bears? Clock is ticking like anything right now!
Article Summary: The 33-year-old edge defender is projected to sign a one-year, $5.7 million contract. Jadeveon Clowney played last season for the Dallas Cowboys, where he played just 13 games and recorded 12 tackles for loss and 22 quarterback pressures. The veteran edge defender has never recorded double-digit sacks, but he has at least 5.5 sacks in the last three seasons.

Let’s presumably give people the credit and just say, ‘Okay, you want to take the WR1 spot away?Name your WR2 right now and tell me how much he makes.’ And then my last question is, ‘Is he better than me?’”The Maryland native openly challenged that there wasn’t a WR2 better than him.But he was WR1 in the New England Patriots, where he caught 85 passes on 100 targets for 1,013 receiving yards and 4 touchdowns in 2025.He even secured an overall 87.5 PFF grade for that season, ranking him 6th among 81 qualified receivers.All this elite performance after he recovered from a brutal 2024 ACL tear.
